info.name: Rare earths

stats.what: of world rare-earth mine output came from China in 2025 (270,000 of about 390,000 t)
of the world's more than 75 million tonnes of reserves are in China

info.uses: Neodymium-iron-boron magnets for electric motors, drones, missile fins and guidance actuators, and aircraft systems.
info.europe: Europe mines almost no rare earths. Estonia is the exception on the processing side: separation in Sillamäe and Europe's largest magnet plant in Narva.

spec.note: The main rare-earth ore at Bayan Obo and Mountain Pass. Forms honey-brown hexagonal plates.

info.uses: Airframes, jet engines, armour, and satellite and launcher structures.
info.europe: Norway's Tellnes is one of Europe's largest titanium mines. Ukraine's ilmenite deposits at Irshansk and Vilnohirsk are a strategic asset; Irshansk restarted in 2023 after a war-related shutdown.

spec.note: Rutile and ilmenite are the main titanium ores. Tellnes and the Ukrainian sites mine ilmenite; Richards Bay produces both.

from this date, tungsten in US defence contracts may not be mined or refined in China, Russia, North Korea or Iran

info.uses: Armour-piercing penetrators, hard-metal cutting tools for the arms industry, and heat-resistant alloys.
info.europe: Europe mines some tungsten in Austria, Portugal and Spain, far less than it uses. China has required export licences for tungsten since February 2025.

spec.note: The ore mined at Mittersill. The other main tungsten ore, wolframite, is mined at Panasqueira.

info.europe: The EU mines almost no antimony. China put antimony exports under licence in August 2024 and banned exports to the US in December 2024; that ban is suspended until 27 November 2026.

spec.note: The main antimony ore, and the name of Idaho's Stibnite project. Grows in long, striated metallic blades.

spec.note: Gallium has no ore of its own. It is recovered from alumina refining and sold as a soft, silvery metal that melts at about 30 °C.

spec.note: Germanium is recovered mainly from zinc ores like this one and from coal fly ash. Kipushi's zinc ore carries germanium.

spec.note: The hard-rock lithium ore mined at Greenbushes. Cínovec's ore is zinnwaldite, a lithium mica named after the village just over the German border.

spec.note: A classic cobalt ore. Most Congolese cobalt comes from copper-cobalt ores instead, mined alongside copper.

spec.note: The main ore at Norilsk. Indonesia's nickel comes mostly from laterite, a weathered red and green soil.

stats.what: of world primary magnesium was made in China in 2025 (950 of about 1,100 kt)
of the EU's primary magnesium comes from China; the EU has no smelter of its own

info.uses: Titanium production (the Kroll process), infrared decoy flares, pyrotechnics and light alloys for airframes and armour.
info.europe: The EU has no primary magnesium smelter. The Critical Raw Materials Act lists magnesium as strategic and aims to keep any single supplier below 65% by 2030.

stats.what: of world electrolytic manganese metal capacity is in China
of world manganese ore came from South Africa in 2025 (7.6 of 20 Mt manganese content)

info.uses: Steel for armour, shells and vehicles (about 90% of all manganese) and battery cathodes for drones and soldier power.
info.europe: Europe has no operating manganese mine. Chvaletice in the Czech Republic, an EU strategic project, plans battery-grade manganese from old tailings, with a feasibility study due in the first half of 2027.

spec.note: A pink manganese carbonate. Most manganese ore is the black oxide pyrolusite, but rhodochrosite shows the metal's colour.

sites.name: Bayan Obo
facts: World's largest known rare-earth deposit
Mines here supplied about 45% of global rare-earth output (2005)
Also the largest known fluorite deposit
sites.why: The geological anchor of China's dominance in rare earths.

sites.name: Mountain Pass
facts: The only rare-earth mining and processing site in the US
The US mined about 51,000 t of rare-earth oxide in 2025 (USGS)
JPMorgan helped arrange $1 billion to expand MP's US magnet production (Fortune, Oct 2026)
sites.why: America's own rare-earth mine; it stopped selling its output to China in 2025.

sites.name: Mount Weld
facts: Mining since 2011 in a 3 km wide carbonatite pipe
Australia mined about 29,000 t of rare-earth oxide in 2025 (USGS)
Concentrate goes to Lynas's plant in Kuantan, Malaysia
sites.why: A supply chain built outside China: mined in Australia, refined in Malaysia.

sites.name: Lynas Advanced Materials Plant
facts: Described as the world's largest rare-earth extraction plant outside China
Target capacity 11,000 t of rare-earth oxides a year; operating since 2012
Licence renewed for ten years in March 2026, without the earlier demand to move cracking and leaching out of Malaysia
sites.why: Refining is the bottleneck in rare earths, and this is one of the few large refineries outside China.

sites.name: Sillamäe separation plant
facts: Former Soviet uranium plant that later moved into niobium, tantalum and rare earths
Produces lanthanum, cerium, praseodymium and neodymium compounds
A heavy rare-earth separation unit is being installed
sites.why: One of the few rare-earth separation plants in the EU.

sites.name: Narva magnet plant
facts: Described as Europe's biggest rare-earth magnet plant, built in about 500 days
First phase: 2,000 t of magnets a year, planned to grow beyond 5,000 t
EU co-funding of $16.9 million
sites.why: Europe's attempt to make the magnets itself instead of importing them from Asia.

sites.name: Panzhihua
facts: Vanadium-titanium magnetite district described as the world's largest titanium resource
About 93% of China's titanium reserves (2007)
Also holds about 63% of China's vanadium reserves
sites.why: A cornerstone of China's titanium industry.

sites.name: Tellnes
facts: Open-pit ilmenite mine, operating since 1960
Reserves over 300 Mt of ore at about 18% titanium
Produced about 580,000 t of ilmenite concentrate in 1999
sites.why: One of Europe's largest titanium mines and a secure source inside NATO.

sites.name: Irshansk
facts: Produces ilmenite concentrate, the raw material for titanium
Idle from October 2022 because of the war, restarted on 5 July 2023
UMCC says it aims to push Russia out of the titanium market
sites.why: Part of the mineral wealth that makes Ukraine strategic for Europe's defence industry.

sites.name: Vilnohirsk
facts: Together with Irshansk, the centre of Ukraine's titanium ore industry
sites.why: Ukraine's second titanium hub, further east and closer to the front line.

sites.name: Richards Bay Minerals
facts: Mines coastal mineral sands and smelts them into titanium slag of about 85% TiO₂
Also produces rutile, zircon and pig iron
About 5,000 workers (2024)
sites.why: One of the largest titanium feedstock sources outside China.

sites.name: Mittersill
facts: Largest scheelite deposit in Europe
About 500,000 t of ore a year, giving roughly 1,200 t of tungsten oxide (2010–2017 data)
Austria mined about 840 t of tungsten in 2025 (USGS)
sites.why: Europe's main tungsten mine, inside the EU.

sites.name: Panasqueira
facts: Mining licence dated 1896
The workforce peaked at nearly 5,800 in 1943
Portugal mined about 700 t of tungsten in 2025 (USGS)
sites.why: One of the longest-running tungsten mines in Europe, inside NATO.

sites.name: Ganzhou tungsten district
facts: Long the centre of China's tungsten industry
China mined about 67,000 of the world's 85,000 t of tungsten in 2025 (USGS)
Exports have needed a Chinese licence since February 2025
sites.why: Shown as a district rather than a single mine: the heart of the supply Western buyers are trying to replace.

sites.name: Xikuangshan
facts: World's largest known antimony deposit
On-site refinery with capacity for 10,000 t of antimony a year
China mined about 40,000 of the world's 110,000 t of antimony in 2025 (USGS)
sites.why: The historic centre of world antimony.

sites.name: Stibnite Gold Project
facts: Expected to hold the only identified antimony reserve in the US
Early construction began in 2026; gold and antimony production planned from 2029
JPMorgan paid $75 million for a 2.7% stake (Fortune, Oct 2026)
sites.why: America's attempt to restart large-scale domestic antimony mining; a small mine in Montana began production in 2025.

sites.name: Metlen gallium project
facts: Planned capacity: 50 t of gallium a year, commercial output from Q3 2027
Selected as a Strategic Project under the EU Critical Raw Materials Act (2025)
EIB approved €90 million, announced 15 January 2026
Gallium was about $3,500/kg in October 2026, up from under $500 when Metlen decided to invest
sites.why: Europe's main bet to cut its reliance on Chinese gallium.

sites.name: Umicore Olen
facts: One of the largest germanium producers and recyclers outside China
More than half its germanium comes from recycled material
Two germanium projects named EU Strategic Projects in March 2025, one for satellite solar-cell substrates
sites.why: Europe's main germanium refiner, supplying optics and space solar cells.

sites.name: Kipushi
facts: Zinc ore grading about 35%, among the richest in the world
The ore also carries germanium
Production restarted in June 2024 after more than 30 years on care and maintenance
sites.why: A zinc mine whose by-products could include germanium for Western buyers.

sites.name: Greenbushes
facts: Described as the largest hard-rock lithium mine in the world
Expansion aims at more than 160,000 t of lithium carbonate equivalent a year
Australia mined about 92,000 t of lithium in 2025 (USGS)
sites.why: Australia mines more lithium than any other country, but most of its concentrate has been refined in China.

sites.name: Salar de Atacama
facts: Brine evaporation ponds large enough to pick out easily from orbit
Held about 27% of the world's lithium reserve base (2008 estimate)
Chile mined about 56,000 t of lithium in 2025, third after Australia and China (USGS)
sites.why: The world's biggest lithium brine operation.

sites.name: Cínovec
facts: Described as Europe's largest lithium resource
EU Strategic Project under the Critical Raw Materials Act (March 2025)
Plans about 37,500 t a year of battery-grade lithium carbonate equivalent, processed at Prunéřov
Environmental impact documentation published in May 2026
sites.why: Czechia's entry in Europe's lithium race, in the Ore Mountains on the German border.

sites.name: Jadar
facts: Jadarite, a lithium-boron mineral, is known only from here
Resource of 118 Mt at 1.8% lithium oxide
Licences revoked in January 2022 after protests; Serbia's Constitutional Court overturned that in July 2024
EU–Serbia raw-materials memorandum signed in July 2024
Rio Tinto put the project on care and maintenance in November 2025, citing slow permitting
sites.why: Potentially one of Europe's biggest lithium sources, and one of its most contested.

sites.name: Tenke Fungurume
facts: Produced 209,120 t of copper and 18,501 t of cobalt in 2021
The DR Congo mined about 230,000 of the world's 310,000 t of cobalt in 2025 (USGS)
sites.why: One of the world's largest cobalt producers, owned by a Chinese group.

sites.name: Mutanda
facts: About 40 km south-east of Kolwezi
Produced 27,300 t of cobalt in 2018
Idled in late 2019 and restarted at the end of 2021
sites.why: A swing producer: when Glencore idled it in 2019, a large share of world cobalt supply went offline.

sites.name: Kokkola cobalt refinery
facts: Bought by Umicore from Freeport in 2019 for $150 million
Capacity 15,000 t a year; described at the time as the largest cobalt refinery outside China
sites.why: Europe's main cobalt refinery, between Congolese ore and European battery plants.

sites.name: Norilsk
facts: Arctic mining and smelting complex on giant nickel-copper-palladium deposits
Nornickel is cited at about 20% of world nickel and 35% of palladium
Russia mined about 200,000 t of nickel in 2025 (USGS)
sites.why: Russia's main source of high-grade nickel and palladium for aerospace alloys.

sites.name: IMIP Morowali
facts: About $34.3 billion invested from 2015 to 2024
About 85,000 workers
Runs largely on captive coal power, including about 2 GW of coal plant
Indonesia mined about 2.6 of the world's 3.9 Mt of nickel in 2025 (USGS)
sites.why: The heart of Indonesia's nickel boom, built largely with Chinese capital.

sites.name: Terrafame
facts: Mines its own ore and extracts the metals by bioleaching
At full capacity makes nickel sulphate for about 1 million EVs and cobalt sulphate for about 300,000
Every production step happens on one site
sites.why: One of Europe's few mine-to-battery-chemical operations.

sites.name: Balama
facts: Capacity of about 350,000 t a year of graphite concentrate
Feeds Syrah's anode plant in Vidalia, Louisiana
Shut from December 2024 after protests; production restarted in June 2025
Mozambique mined about 60,000 t of graphite in 2025 (USGS)
sites.why: One of the few large graphite mines outside China.

sites.name: Vittangi
facts: Graphite mine planned at Vittangi, with an anode refinery at the port of Luleå
Designed for 19,500 t a year of battery anode material
Talga targets a final investment decision in early 2027
sites.why: One of Europe's most advanced plans to make battery anodes from its own graphite.

sites.name: Fugu and Yulin smelters
facts: Centre of China's magnesium smelting (the Pidgeon process)
China made about 950 of the world's 1,100 kt of primary magnesium in 2025 (USGS)
sites.why: Most of the world's magnesium is made here.

sites.name: Dead Sea Magnesium
facts: Electrolytic magnesium from Dead Sea brine
Israel produced about 20 kt of magnesium in 2025 (USGS)
sites.why: One of the few large smelters outside China.

sites.name: RIMA magnesium
facts: Brazil produced about 20 kt of magnesium in 2025 (USGS)
sites.why: The only primary magnesium in the Americas still running.

sites.name: Solikamsk magnesium works
facts: Russia produced about 60 kt of magnesium in 2025 (USGS)
Magnesium here also feeds titanium production
sites.why: Russia is the second producer after China.

sites.name: Ust-Kamenogorsk titanium-magnesium plant
facts: Kazakhstan produced about 13 kt of magnesium in 2025 (USGS)
Makes magnesium and titanium sponge on one site
sites.why: Shows how titanium depends on magnesium.

sites.name: US Magnesium (idle)
facts: The only US primary magnesium smelter stopped producing in 2022
Its operator filed for bankruptcy in September 2025 (USGS)
sites.why: Why the West now buys its magnesium from China.

sites.name: Kalahari Manganese Field
facts: South Africa mined 7.6 of the world's 20 Mt of manganese in 2025 (USGS)
Holds about a third of world reserves
sites.why: The largest manganese source on Earth.

sites.name: Moanda manganese mine
facts: Gabon mined about 5.0 Mt of manganese in 2025, second after South Africa (USGS)
High-grade ore, shipped through Owendo
sites.why: One of the richest manganese deposits.

sites.name: Nsuta manganese mine
facts: Ghana mined about 2.0 Mt of manganese in 2025 (USGS)
sites.why: Africa's fast-growing third producer.

sites.name: Groote Eylandt
facts: Restarted in May 2025 after a cyclone stopped it in 2024 (USGS)
Australia mined about 1.6 Mt of manganese in 2025
sites.why: Shows how one storm can cut supply.

sites.name: Manganese Triangle refineries
facts: China holds over 95% of world electrolytic manganese metal capacity (SMM)
The cluster spans Guangxi, Guizhou and Hunan
sites.why: Where almost all refined manganese is made.

sites.name: Chvaletice manganese project
facts: Plans battery-grade manganese from old mine tailings
EU strategic project; feasibility study due in the first half of 2027
sites.why: Europe's best chance of its own manganese.

scenarios.title: China stops exporting gallium
scenarios.prec: China put gallium under export licences in August 2023 and banned exports to the US in December 2024. That ban is suspended until 27 November 2026.

scenarios.title: China stops exporting rare-earth magnets
scenarios.prec: China's October 2025 controls on rare-earth magnets, equipment and technology are paused until 10 January 2027. The EU imports 98% of its rare-earth magnets from China.

scenarios.title: China stops exporting graphite anodes
scenarios.prec: China has required licences for some graphite since December 2023. Its October 2025 controls on anode materials are paused until 10 January 2027.

scenarios.title: China stops exporting germanium
scenarios.prec: Germanium has needed a Chinese export licence since August 2023, and exports to the US were banned in December 2024 (suspended until 27 November 2026). China's germanium metal exports fell 60% in January–September 2025.

scenarios.title: China stops exporting tungsten
scenarios.prec: China has required export licences for tungsten since February 2025. From 1 January 2027, US defence contracts may not use tungsten mined or refined in China.

scenarios.title: China stops exporting antimony
scenarios.prec: China put antimony under licences in August 2024 and banned exports to the US in December 2024. The US only began mining antimony again in 2025.

scenarios.title: The DR Congo halts cobalt exports
scenarios.prec: The DR Congo suspended cobalt exports in February 2025 and replaced the ban with quotas: 87,000 t of cobalt for 2026, plus up to 9,600 t of strategic quota.

scenarios.title: Indonesia cuts nickel ore output
scenarios.prec: Indonesia set its 2026 nickel ore quota at 290–300 Mt after an October 2026 revision, against about 320 Mt mined in 2025.

scenarios.title: China stops exporting lithium chemicals
scenarios.prec: China's October 2025 controls on lithium-battery and cathode materials are paused until 10 January 2027.
